Synopsis:
Asian wheat importers are scrambling to replace delayed or cancelled Black Sea (Russian/Ukrainian) wheat cargoes due to attacks on port infrastructure and vessels. At least 500,000 MT of Australian and Argentine wheat has been purchased as an alternative, at a significant price premium ($310–$330/t CFR vs. $260–$280/t for Black Sea). CBOT wheat futures have risen ~35% since late June. Approximately 2.0–2.5 MMT of Black Sea wheat booked for July–September shipment is at risk of non-delivery, representing 30–50% of regional import demand. Buyers are also using container shipments to meet immediate needs while deferring Black Sea arrivals.
